solar-panel.definition: A device with linked semiconductor cells that changes sunlight directly into electrical power.
solar-panel.exampleUsage: The solar panel converted sunlight into electrical energy.

inverter.definition: An electrical converter that converts direct current into alternating current.

battery-storage.definition: A system that stores electrical energy in batteries for later use.

charge-controller.definition: An electronic device that regulates electrical energy moving between solar panels, batteries, and loads.
charge-controller.exampleUsage: The charge controller regulated charging according to the battery system’s specified limits.

mounting-frame.definition: A supporting structure used to hold equipment securely in a chosen position.
mounting-frame.exampleUsage: The solar panels were fastened to a metal mounting frame.

tracker.definition: A mechanism that adjusts solar-panel orientation to follow the sun’s position.

junction-box.definition: An enclosed box that protects points where electrical wires or circuits are joined.
junction-box.exampleUsage: The technician inspected the sealed junction box.

combiner-box.definition: An electrical enclosure that combines outputs from several solar-panel strings into fewer circuits.
combiner-box.exampleUsage: The combiner box collects power from several panel strings.

transformer.definition: An electrical device by which alternating current of one voltage is changed to another voltage.
transformer.exampleUsage: The transformer changed voltage within the site’s designed AC system.

grid-connection.definition: The electrical link between a power-generating system and the public electricity network.
grid-connection.exampleUsage: The grid connection allows the solar farm to supply electricity to the network.

drill.definition: A tool with a rotating bit used for making holes.
drill.exampleUsage: The qualified worker selected a drill suitable for the material and task.

wrench.definition: A tool used for turning nuts, bolts, or pipes.
wrench.exampleUsage: The mechanic selected a wrench of the appropriate size for the nut.

wire-cutter.definition: A hand tool with two sharp edges designed to cut wire.
wire-cutter.exampleUsage: The technician selected a wire cutter suited to the material.

crimping-tool.definition: A hand tool used to press a connector tightly onto a wire or cable.
crimping-tool.exampleUsage: The technician used the correct crimping tool for the cable connector.

cable-tie.definition: A plastic strip that tightens around cables to hold them together.

conduit.definition: A passage (a pipe or tunnel) through which water or electric wires can pass.

ground-rod.definition: A metal electrode installed in the earth as part of a professionally designed grounding system.

multimeter.definition: A portable instrument that tests several features of electricity, including voltage, current, and resistance, in a circuit.
multimeter.exampleUsage: The trained technician selected a suitable multimeter for the specified electrical measurement.

level.definition: A tool used to check whether a surface is horizontal or vertical.
level.exampleUsage: The technician checked the bracket’s orientation with a spirit level.

ladder.definition: A structure with side supports and steps or rungs used for climbing.

control-room.definition: A room where operators monitor solar-farm equipment and operating conditions.

security-fence.definition: A barrier built to prevent unauthorized entry into an area.

access-road.definition: A road leading into a site, such as a solar farm.

gate.definition: A movable barrier controlling entry through a fence or enclosure.
gate.exampleUsage: The gate controlled access to the fenced site.

weather-station.definition: A site in a network of stations that measures and records meteorological conditions.

camera.definition: A device that captures still images or video.

substation.definition: An electrical installation that transforms, switches, or distributes power between parts of a network.

cable-tray.definition: A support structure that holds and routes electrical cables.

lightning-rod.definition: A metal conductor that helps protect a building from lightning.

grounding-system.definition: A professionally designed arrangement connecting specified equipment to earth for electrical protection.

sunlight.definition: The light and energy that come from the sun.

solar-cell.definition: A photovoltaic device that converts light into electrical energy.
solar-cell.exampleUsage: A solar cell converted incoming light into electrical energy.

electricity.definition: Energy made available by the flow of electric charge through a conductor.

voltage.definition: The electrical potential difference between two points, measured in volts.

current.definition: The flow of electric charge through a circuit, measured in amperes.

watt.definition: A unit of power equal to 1 joule per second.

kilowatt.definition: A unit of power equal to 1000 watts.

energy-meter.definition: A device that measures the amount of electrical energy used or produced.

power-line.definition: A cable that carries electricity from generating stations to homes, businesses, and other users.

distribution-panel.definition: A board that divides electrical power among different circuits.

cleaning-brush.definition: A brush used to remove dirt from a surface.

water-hose.definition: A flexible tube used to carry water to a place.

inspection-drone.definition: A drone used to inspect equipment or an area from the air.

thermal-camera.definition: A camera that shows temperature differences using infrared light.

safety-vest.definition: A garment designed to make its wearer more visible under its specified conditions.

hard-hat.definition: A rigid protective helmet selected for specified workplace head hazards.

gloves.definition: Protective hand coverings selected for the professional work being performed.

tool-belt.definition: A belt worn around the waist keeps hand tools close in pockets and loops. It is useful for carpentry, repairs, and crafts.
tool-belt.exampleUsage: The tool belt kept the worker’s tools close to hand.

logbook.definition: A record of operating events, observations, inspections, or maintenance.

clipboard.definition: A small writing board with a clip at the top for holding papers.

open-field.definition: An open area of land with few buildings or trees.

clear-sky.definition: A sky with little or no cloud cover in the described conditions.

cloud.definition: A visible collection of tiny water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere.

sunrise.definition: The time when the sun first appears in the sky.

sunset.definition: The time or event when the sun disappears below the horizon at the end of the day.

grassland.definition: Land where grass or grasslike vegetation grows and is the dominant form of plant life.

wildflower.definition: A wild flower that grows without being planted.

bird.definition: An animal with feathers, wings, and a beak.
bird.exampleUsage: A bird flew above the fenced solar site.

fence-post.definition: A post anchored in the ground supports the rails, boards, wires, mesh, or panels that make up a fence.

battery.exampleUsage: The battery stored electrical energy in the site’s supported storage system.

cable.definition: A conductor for transmitting electrical or optical signals or electric power.

mounting-rack.definition: A frame that holds equipment such as solar panels in place.

meter.definition: A measuring instrument recording a quantity such as electrical energy.

grid.definition: A system of high tension cables by which electrical power is distributed throughout a region.

charge.definition: To supply electrical energy to a rechargeable battery for storage.

discharge.definition: To release stored electrical energy from a battery into a load.

clean-energy.definition: Energy associated with lower emissions or pollution; environmental impacts depend on the technology and its full life cycle.

renewable.definition: Able to be replaced naturally as it is used, like sunlight or wind.

carbon.definition: An abundant nonmetallic tetravalent element occurring in three allotropic forms: amorphous carbon and graphite and diamond.

emission.definition: A release of a substance, such as a greenhouse gas, into the environment.

sustainability.definition: Using resources in ways intended to meet present needs while preserving future ability to meet them.

efficiency.definition: The ratio of the output to the input of any system.

conservation.definition: Reducing unnecessary resource use and protecting resources from avoidable loss.

recycle.definition: To process discarded material so it can be used again.
